title: One year after the October 2025 Gaza ceasefire, Israeli strikes continue and disarmament has not begun
body:
On 10 October 2026, AFP marked one year since the ceasefire that US President Donald Trump declared the end of the Gaza war. It listed what had been achieved: Hamas freed the 20 remaining living hostages three days after the deal was announced, there had been no Hamas rocket attacks on Israel from Gaza for a year, and the US military had set up a command post with allies near the Gaza border to monitor the truce.

AFP said many promises were unfulfilled. Israel had reduced its attacks but still struck Gaza nearly every day, and the Gaza health ministry, whose figures the UN considers accurate, said about 1,450 Palestinians had been killed since the ceasefire. The ceasefire allowed Israeli forces to hold 53 percent of Gaza, and according to official accounts they now controlled about 70 percent. Hamas said in July it would give up its weapons but had not begun disarming, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu demanded verifiable decommissioning of every weapon before any Israeli withdrawal.

Hamas announced in July that it was disbanding its governing body, but it effectively remained in charge of security, and Ali Shaath, the technocrat heading the new administration committee, had kept a low profile. Trump promised 10 billion dollars in US funding for reconstruction in January and Gulf allies pledged more, but no money was known to have reached Gaza reconstruction. In September the Board of Peace proposed a 2.45 billion dollar six-month recovery plan. Netanyahu said on the anniversary of the attack that 4,000 of 6,000 Hamas fighters had been killed, a figure the report did not verify.
